partners.mechanism_chain: CYP4V2 (HGNC:24670) —DISRUPTS→ Heme biosynthesis and CYP450 activity (REACT:R-HSA-6207711); Heme biosynthesis and CYP450 activity (REACT:R-HSA-6207711) —LEADS_TO→ Crystalline deposits in cornea and retina (HP:0030054); FDX2 (HGNC:3470) —DISRUPTS→ Mitochondrial electron transport chain (REACT:R-HSA-3998900); Mitochondrial electron transport chain (REACT:R-HSA-3998900) —LEADS_TO→ Mitochondrial myopathy (HP:0003198); Mitochondrial electron transport chain (REACT:R-HSA-3998900) —LEADS_TO→ Optic atrophy (HP:0000648); Mitochondrial electron transport chain (REACT:R-HSA-3998900) —LEADS_TO→ Leukoencephalopathy (HP:0012734). Loss-of-function mutations in CYP4V2 disrupt heme biosynthesis and downstream CYP450 activity, leading to crystalline deposits in ocular tissues. Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in FDX2 disrupt the mitochondrial electron transport chain, resulting in myopathy, optic atrophy, and leukoencephalopathy. The shared mechanism lies in the convergence on mitochondrial dysfunction, as CYP4V2's role in heme synthesis is indirectly linked to mitochondrial respiration, and FDX2 directly impacts the electron transport chain.

falsification.text: Discovery of pathogenic variants in CYP4V2 in patients with mitochondrial myopathy, episodic, with optic atrophy and reversible leukoencephalopathy, or conversely, pathogenic variants in FDX2 in patients with Bietti crystalline corneoretinal dystrophy, would falsify the hypothesis of a shared primary genetic cause. Furthermore, if molecular studies demonstrate completely independent functional pathways for CYP4V2 and FDX2 with no overlap in downstream mitochondrial processes, the hypothesis would be refuted.
